gloss: to drill into; to instill; to train thoroughly

definitions.gloss: to drill into; to instill; to train thoroughly; to teach persistently
definitions.explanation: To teach something so repeatedly and thoroughly that it becomes deeply ingrained. The ～{込|こ}む suffix adds a sense of thoroughness and persistence to the base verb {教|おし}える.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}にマナーを{教|おし}え{込|こ}む。
examples.english: To instill manners in a child.

examples.japanese: {基本|きほん}を{徹底的|てっていてき}に{教|おし}え{込|こ}まれた。
examples.english: The basics were thoroughly drilled into me.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}に{小|ちい}さい{頃|ころ}から「{感謝|かんしゃ}の{気持|きも}ちを{忘|わす}れるな」と{教|おし}え{込|こ}まれた。
examples.english: My grandmother drilled into me from a young age to never forget to be grateful.

notes:
A compound verb: {教|おし}える (to teach) + {込|こ}む (into, thoroughly). The ～{込|こ}む suffix conveys the idea of something being driven in deeply through repetition.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- マナーを{教|おし}え{込|こ}む — to instill manners
- {基本|きほん}を{教|おし}え{込|こ}む — to drill in the basics
- {小|ちい}さい{頃|ころ}から{教|おし}え{込|こ}まれる — to have something drilled in from childhood

USAGE:
Often used in the passive ({教|おし}え{込|こ}まれる) to describe values or skills that were instilled by parents, teachers, or mentors. Can have a slightly forceful nuance — the teaching is persistent and thorough, not casual.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {教|おし}える — to teach (neutral; {教|おし}え{込|こ}む implies repeated, thorough instruction)
- {叩|たた}き{込|こ}む — to hammer in, to beat into (stronger, more physical nuance)
- {仕込|しこ}む — to train, to coach (often used for apprentices or animals)
